title: Decir gracias en la ronda
caption:
En una ronda de mate, decir "gracias" es lo peor que podés hacer 🧉😅
¿A vos también te pasó? Contalo 👇

story.logline: On his first visit to his girlfriend's family, a young man politely says "gracias" when he returns the mate; the cebador (her father) takes it as "no more" and skips him round after round until the grandmother whispers the rule; he jumps onto his chair and shouts that he wants more, and the suegro serves him mate after mate.
timeline: Shots 1-4: a Sunday afternoon about 16:00, sun.
Shot 5: time-lapse, about an hour later, 17:30, dusk light; the termo is empty.
Shots 6-9: right after, dusk; shot 8 with a second termo (red) the suegro fetched.
links: 1 is a wide preview of the moment told in 2-3.
2 -> 3: he holds the mate, then drinks and gives it back saying gracias.
3 -> 4: the cebador reads gracias as "no more" and skips him.
4 -> 5: the round goes on for an hour until the termo is empty.
5 -> 6: the abuela, sitting next to him, has watched and tells him the rule.
6 -> 7: he understands and shouts that he wants more.
7 -> 8: the suegro gets the second termo and serves him again and again.
8 -> 9: everybody laughs; he is part of the ronda now.

places.patio: one patio; round table in the middle; seated: vos (front right), abuela (to his right, back right), novia (back left), cuñado (front left); the cebador walks on an outer circle around the chairs

knowledge: vos does not know the rule until shot 6.
The family knows from shot 3 what his gracias means.

vos.looks: short neat dark hair, light blue shirt, beige trousers

suegro.looks: black boina, thick moustache, dark red polo, grey trousers, green termo (red one later)

abuela.looks: grey bun, round glasses, purple cardigan, grey skirt

cunado.looks: dark curly hair, green football shirt

patio.desc: family patio: brick floor circle, grass, white back wall with bushes, lemon tree, parrilla with smoke, side wall with door, string lights, round table with white cloth, yerba pack and medialunas, four low chairs, a sleeping dog, plant pots
patio.light: shots 1-4 sun from the front left; 5-9 dusk, orange, glowing bulbs

segments.text: En una ronda de mate, decir gracias es lo peor que podés hacer.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "En una ronda de mate, decir gracias es lo peor que podés hacer." About 3.8 seconds. Hook.

What the viewer must understand without sound: a sunny family patio, a ronda of mate around a round table, everyone relaxed; the mate goes to the young man in the light blue shirt, he drinks, gives it back with a polite nod, and in that very moment the cebador lifts one eyebrow and the whole table freezes for a beat. Something just went wrong, and the viewer wants to know what. Context (family ronda), curiosity (what did he do?) and the snapback (polite = wrong) must all be in these four seconds.

Why this picture: a ronda is a circle, and a circle is what 3D does best. We open high and wide, looking down at the whole circle like a drone, so the viewer sees all five people and the patio in one look, then the camera sinks and swings around to the young man while the mate travels to him. The movement of the camera follows the movement of the mate.

The set in this shot. A family patio in the afternoon. Under the table a round floor of terracotta bricks, about eight metres across, laid in rows of warm orange, slightly different tones. Around it short green grass. At the back a low white wall with a terracotta cap, dark green bushes in front of it; on the left behind the table a lemon tree with yellow lemons; at the back right a brick parrilla with glowing embers, five chorizos on the grill and white smoke curling up into the sky. On the left a white side wall with a brown wooden door. Over the patio a string of light bulbs in yellow, pink and light blue hangs in a soft curve from left to right, the bulbs glowing faintly in the daylight. In the centre a round wooden table with a white tablecloth; on it a red-and-white yerba pack lying on its side and a white plate with two medialunas. Around the table four low wooden chairs with straw seats, one for each seated person, all turned towards the centre. In the front right on the bricks a toy dog with light brown fur sleeps curled up, chin on the floor. Terracotta pots with round green plants stand in the corners. The sky is clear blue with a few soft white clouds; the sun comes from the front left, so faces are lit and the shadows fall back and to the right.

The people. Five toy figures with big round heads and ball hands.
Vos, the young man (about 25): short dark brown hair combed neatly for the visit, a light blue shirt with buttons, beige trousers, sits at the front right of the table (as seen from the camera), turned to the centre, back straight, hands on his knees, a nervous polite smile.
The suegro, his girlfriend's father and the cebador (about 58): grey-brown short hair under a black boina, a thick moustache, a dark red polo shirt, grey trousers; he does not sit, he stands at the back of the table with the green termo under his left arm and the mate in his right hand.
The abuela (about 82): grey hair in a bun, round glasses, a purple cardigan, a grey skirt; she sits at the back right, directly to the right of vos.
The novia (about 24): long dark brown hair in a ponytail, a yellow T-shirt, jeans; she sits at the back left.
The cuñado (about 30): dark curly hair, a green football shirt, dark shorts; he sits at the front left, leaning back with his arms crossed.

Movements, beat by beat.
At 0.0 the suegro stands at the back right of the table between the abuela and vos, the mate in his right hand held out towards vos, the termo in his left arm. His face is friendly, eyes half closed in the calm of an old cebador.
At 0.1 vos turns his head to the suegro and reaches out his left hand to the side; the mate travels from the suegro's hand to his on a small arc (the hand-over takes about a third of a second).
At 0.3 vos brings the mate to his mouth and drinks: two quick sips, eyes closed, cheeks pulled in. Everyone else watches him: the abuela turns her head to him, the novia smiles at him with her chin on her hand, the cuñado raises his chin.
At 0.62 vos lowers the mate, smiles wide, nods once with his whole upper body and holds the mate out to the suegro: the mate travels back. This is the moment he says "gracias".
At 0.75 the suegro takes it and stops. One eyebrow goes up (sly face), his head tilts. The abuela's eyes go to the cuñado, the cuñado's eyes go to the novia: a silent look around the table.
At 0.9 the dog lifts its head and looks at vos too.

Camera. Starts high and wide in front of the table, slightly to the right (about 20 degrees around), 4.6 metres away, 3.2 metres up, looking down at the centre of the table: the whole circle and most of the patio are in the picture. During the shot it sinks to 2.2 metres and moves closer to 3.4 metres while swinging to about 40 degrees, so that at the end vos and the suegro fill the middle of the frame and the faces of all five are readable. The movement is smooth and slow, never a jump. Nobody's head is cut.

Timing on the words: "En una ronda de mate" = the wide circle, the mate arrives at vos. "decir gracias" = he drinks and gives it back with the nod. "es lo peor" = the eyebrow and the silent looks. "que podés hacer" = the dog looks up.

Sounds: birds, the faint sizzle of the parrilla, a soft "slurp" for the sip, a small comic "dun" on the eyebrow.

The feeling: warm and pleasant at first, then a tiny chill: the polite word was the mistake.

Continuity to the next shot: same moment; everyone keeps looking at vos.

segments.text: Primera vez en lo de tu novia: toda la familia te está mirando.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "Primera vez en lo de tu novia: toda la familia te está mirando." About 3.4 seconds.

What the viewer must understand without sound: this is his first visit, he is nervous, and every single person at the table is watching him. The pressure has to be physical: four heads turned to one face, a sweat drop, even the dog.

Link to the shot before: the hook showed the moment from far away. Now we go back a few seconds to the moment just before: the suegro has just handed him the mate, vos holds it in his left hand and has not drunk yet. The time on the clock of the story is the same afternoon, the same light.

The set in this shot. We are now low and close at the front right of the table, at the height of the seated heads. Behind vos the brick floor runs back, the white back wall with the terracotta cap, the bushes, the lemon tree out of focus at the left edge, the parrilla smoke rising at the right edge. The string lights cross the top of the frame. The table edge with the white tablecloth is in the lower left corner, the yerba pack and the plate with medialunas visible on it. The sunlight comes from the front left and lights vos' face fully.

The people.
Vos sits on his chair at the front right, turned to the centre of the table, so we see him three quarters from the front. He holds the mate in his left hand in front of his chest. His back is too straight, his shoulders are pulled up. Face: big worried eyes, eyebrows pulled up in the middle, a stiff smile that does not reach the eyes. A sweat drop runs down from his temple twice during the shot.
The abuela sits to his right, very close; she has turned her whole head to him and looks at him over her glasses, lips pressed, curious.
The novia sits at the back left; she props her chin on her hand and smiles at him, proud and a bit amused.
The cuñado sits at the front left, leaning back, arms crossed, chin up; he narrows his eyes at vos like a judge.
The suegro stands at the back right behind the abuela with the termo under his arm, looking down at vos with a calm, unreadable face.
The dog lifts its head off the floor halfway through the shot and stares at vos too, ears up.

Movements, beat by beat.
At 0.0 everyone is already looking at vos. Vos looks down at the mate.
At 0.25 vos lifts his eyes and looks from one face to the next: first the abuela, then the suegro; with each look his smile gets stiffer. The first sweat drop starts.
At 0.5 the dog lifts its head. Vos swallows (his head dips once).
At 0.75 vos looks straight into the camera for half a second: "help".

Camera. A low, close shot at seated eye height, from the front right of the table (about 55 degrees around), 2.0 metres from vos, moving slowly in to 1.6 metres during the shot. Vos' face is in the upper middle of the frame; the abuela is next to him at the right edge, the novia and the cuñado are visible but softer in the background. The slow push in makes the pressure grow.

Timing: "Primera vez en lo de tu novia" = vos looks down at the mate. "toda la familia" = his eyes go from face to face. "te está mirando" = the dog lifts its head, he looks into the camera.

Effects and sounds: two small light blue sweat drops at his temple; a quiet clock-like tick under the voice, a gulp.

The feeling: the viewer remembers their own first visit and squirms with him.

Continuity: in the next shot he drinks this mate and gives it back.

segments.text: Tomás, devolvés el mate y, educado, decís: gracias.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "Tomás, devolvés el mate y, educado, decís: gracias." About 3.6 seconds.

What the viewer must understand without sound: he drinks, gives the mate back with a polite nod and a smile, and the reactions show that this was a mistake: the suegro's eyebrow goes up and the abuela and the cuñado exchange a look. The viewer who knows the rule laughs; the one who does not wants to know why.

Link to the shot before: he is holding the mate; now he drinks it.

The set: the same patio, seen from the front, a little higher than before, so that vos and the suegro are both in the frame with the table between them. The tablecloth, the yerba pack, the medialunas, the string lights at the top, the parrilla smoke at the back right, the lemon tree at the back left.

The people and their movements.
At 0.0 vos brings the mate to his mouth with the left hand and drinks: eyes closed, cheeks pulled in, two sips. His other hand rests on his knee.
At 0.4 he lowers the mate, opens his eyes and smiles widely, proud that he did it well.
At 0.55 he holds the mate out towards the suegro and nods twice with his whole upper body: this is "gracias". The mate travels from his hand to the suegro's right hand on a small arc.
At 0.7 the suegro takes it and freezes: his right eyebrow rises, the moustache twitches, he tilts his head and looks at vos with a sly face.
At 0.75 the abuela turns her head slowly from vos to the cuñado; the cuñado turns his head to the abuela; for a moment they look at each other with the same sly face. The novia covers her mouth with her hand, eyes wide.
At 0.9 vos, who noticed nothing, keeps smiling at everybody.

Camera. A medium shot from the front, about 30 degrees to the right of the table axis, 2.8 metres away, at 1.5 metres height, looking at a point between vos and the suegro. Both faces and the mate are always in the frame; the abuela and the cuñado are visible for the exchanged look. A very slow drift to the left during the shot.

Timing: "Tomás" = the sip. "devolvés el mate" = the mate travels back. "y, educado," = his nod and smile. "decís: gracias" = the eyebrow and the exchanged looks.

Sounds: a slurp, a small polite "mm", a comic "dun-dun" on the eyebrow.

Facts: in an Argentine ronda, saying "gracias" when you return the mate means that you do not want any more. Correct.

Continuity: the suegro now has the mate and the termo; in the next shot he starts serving the others.

segments.text: Y desde ese momento, el mate te esquiva.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "Y desde ese momento, el mate te esquiva." About 3.6 seconds.

What the viewer must understand without sound: the suegro walks around the table serving everyone one after the other, and when he comes to vos he simply walks past him. Vos even raises his hand a little, and the suegro does not stop. The mate literally goes around him.

Why this picture: the circle again, now in motion. The camera turns around the whole table together with the suegro, so the viewer feels the round being completed without vos.

The set: the whole patio as in the hook, seen from 2.4 metres height; as the camera circles, the background changes: the parrilla with smoke, the white back wall and bushes, the lemon tree, the side wall with the door, the sleeping dog in the front.

Movements, beat by beat.
At 0.0 the suegro stands behind the novia (back left), pours hot water from the termo into the mate (the termo tilts, a thin stream), then hands her the mate. She drinks and gives it back.
At 0.3 he walks around the table to the cuñado (front left) and does the same. The cuñado takes it with one hand without uncrossing his legs, drinks, gives it back.
At 0.55 the suegro walks on to the front right, right past vos. Vos lifts his left hand halfway, opens his mouth to say something; his face shows hope. The suegro does not even look at him; he walks on, humming, eyes on the mate.
At 0.7 he stops behind the abuela (back right), pours, hands her the mate. Vos slowly lowers his hand, his face falls (sad), shoulders sink.
At 0.9 the abuela drinks with relish; vos looks at her mate.

Camera. An orbit around the table: it starts behind-left (about 300 degrees), 3.4 metres from the centre, 2.4 metres high, and turns smoothly about 120 degrees during the shot, always looking at the centre of the table at 0.7 metres height. The suegro stays roughly in the middle of the frame because the camera turns with him.

Timing: "Y desde ese momento" = serving the novia. "el mate" = serving the cuñado. "te esquiva" = he walks past vos, the hand goes up and down.

Sounds: footsteps on the bricks, the pour, a small hum of the suegro, a sad "wah" when the hand goes down.

The gag: the hand that goes up full of hope and is ignored.

Continuity: the round goes on; in the next shot time passes.

segments.text: Pasa una vuelta, pasan dos, y se termina el termo.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "Pasa una vuelta, pasan dos, y se termina el termo." About 3.4 seconds.

What the viewer must understand without sound: time passes (the light turns orange, the string lights glow brighter), the suegro keeps circling, vos sinks lower and lower on his chair, and finally the termo is empty: the suegro turns it upside down and only one drop falls.

Why this picture: from straight above the round becomes a clock: the suegro walking around the table is the hand of the clock, and the light changing is the time passing.

The set: seen from above: the round table with the white cloth in the centre, the four chairs and seated people around it, the brick circle, the edge of the grass; the dog at the front right curled up asleep again. The light is now late afternoon: warm orange, long soft shadows, the bulbs of the string light glowing.

Movements.
At 0.0 the suegro walks a full circle around the table, fast, like in a time-lapse; at each person except vos he stops for a moment and the mate moves in and out of their hands.
Vos, as the suegro passes him, leans more and more: at the start he sits upright, at the end he hangs on the chair, head down, face sad.
At 0.75 the suegro stands at the back of the table, lifts the termo and turns it upside down; a single drop falls into the mate. He shakes the termo once and looks into it with one eye.

Camera. High above the table looking almost straight down (4.5 metres up, a little in front), then slowly lowering and tilting forward to 3.2 metres while turning about 40 degrees, so at the end we see the empty termo and vos slumped.

Timing: "Pasa una vuelta" = the first fast circle. "pasan dos" = the second. "y se termina el termo" = the upside-down termo and the single drop.

Sounds: fast footsteps, a ticking clock, a single "plip" of the drop.

Continuity: dusk light stays for the rest of the reel; the termo is empty.

segments.text: Hasta que la abuela te dice al oído: gracias es que no querés más.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "Hasta que la abuela te dice al oído: gracias es que no querés más." About 4.0 seconds.

What the viewer must understand without sound: the abuela, who sits right next to him, leans over, covers her mouth with her hand and whispers into his ear; his eyes become huge as he understands. This is where the viewer learns the rule.

Link to the shot before: the termo is empty, vos is slumped. The abuela has watched it all and takes pity on him.

The set: a close two-shot from the front right; behind them the white back wall and the bushes in orange evening light, the glowing string lights above, the parrilla smoke now pink in the sunset, the lemon tree dark.

Movements.
At 0.0 vos sits slumped, looking at the floor (sad face).
At 0.15 the abuela turns to him, leans her upper body towards him and raises her hand to her mouth like a little wall; her eyes look sideways at the suegro to check he is not listening.
At 0.35 she whispers; vos turns his ear to her, still sad.
At 0.65 his eyes open wide, his eyebrows fly up, his mouth falls open (surprised); he slowly turns his face to her.
At 0.85 she nods twice, wisely, eyes closed, lips pressed: "así es, nene".

Camera. Close on both faces, from about 70 degrees around (front right), 1.8 metres away, 1.3 metres high, looking at the point between their heads. A very slow push in.

Timing: "Hasta que la abuela" = she turns and leans. "te dice al oído" = the hand at the mouth, the whisper. "gracias es que" = his eyes start to open. "no querés más" = full surprise, her nods.

Sounds: a soft "psst", a whisper sound, a "ding" of understanding.

Facts: correct rule (saying gracias = no more for me).

Continuity: next he jumps up.

segments.text: Te subís a la silla y gritás: ¡no, gracias no, quiero más!

shots.direction:
Sentence: "Te subís a la silla y gritás: ¡no, gracias no, quiero más!" About 3.8 seconds.

What the viewer must understand without sound: he climbs onto his chair, raises both arms and shouts; everyone at the table jumps, the dog jumps up and barks. Pure slapstick.

The set: the evening patio seen from low in front of the table (the camera near the floor looking up), so vos on the chair stands against the orange sky and the string lights. The table edge in the foreground.

Movements.
At 0.0 vos stands up from the chair in one jerk.
At 0.15 he steps up onto the seat of the chair; now he towers over the table.
At 0.3 both arms go up high, fists open, his mouth wide open shouting (scream face), his whole body shaking a little.
At 0.35 everyone else jumps on their chairs (a small jump), faces shocked; the suegro almost drops the empty termo; the novia puts both hands on her cheeks.
At 0.5 the dog jumps up on its feet, head high.
At 0.8 vos stays up there with his arms high, breathing hard.

Camera. Low angle from the front, about 20 degrees around, 2.6 metres away, 0.8 metres high, looking up at vos (look point at his chest). A short shake when he shouts.

Timing: "Te subís a la silla" = standing up and stepping up. "y gritás" = arms up. "¡no, gracias no, quiero más!" = everyone jumps, the dog jumps up.

Sounds: chair scrape, a big shout under the voice, a dog bark, a cymbal crash.

Continuity: in the next shot the suegro reacts.

segments.text: Y ahora tu suegro te ceba uno atrás del otro.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "Y ahora tu suegro te ceba uno atrás del otro." About 3.4 seconds.

What the viewer must understand without sound: the suegro got the message: he has a new full termo and now he stands next to vos and hands him mate after mate, faster and faster; vos drinks each one, his cheeks fuller each time; everyone laughs.

Logic: the termo was empty; the suegro has fetched the second termo (a red one) from the parrilla side. That is why it is red now.

The set: medium shot of vos (sitting again) and the suegro next to him at the front right; behind them the evening patio, glowing bulbs, the others laughing at the table.

Movements.
At 0.0 the suegro stands next to vos with a red termo under his arm and the mate, a big grin under the moustache.
From 0.1 to 0.9 he hands vos the mate three times: each time the mate travels to vos' left hand, vos drinks it in one go (sip face), gives it back, and immediately it comes again. The rhythm speeds up.
The others laugh (laugh faces), the cuñado slaps the table, the novia laughs with her hand on her chest.
At 0.9 vos holds up one finger: "wait".

Camera. Medium shot from the front right, 2.4 metres away, 1.4 metres high, looking between vos and the suegro.

Sounds: fast slurps in rhythm, laughter.

Continuity: the last shot pulls back from this scene.

segments.text: ¿A vos también te pasó? Contalo en los comentarios.

shots.direction:
Sentence: "¿A vos también te pasó? Contalo en los comentarios." About 3.6 seconds, then the poll.

What the viewer must understand without sound: the whole family laughs together at the table in the evening light, vos is part of the ronda now; the question invites the viewer to tell their own story.

The set: the full patio at dusk, wide: the round table in the centre, the glowing string lights, the pink smoke of the parrilla, the lemon tree, the dog wagging its tail next to vos.

Movements: everyone laughs (laugh faces), the suegro pats vos on the shoulder, vos smiles with full cheeks holding the mate, the dog sits up.

Camera. Pulls back and rises: from 3.5 metres and 2.0 metres height to 5.5 metres and 3.5 metres height, turning from 30 to 60 degrees around the table. The poll appears in the lower part of the frame at about 0.55 of the shot and never covers a face.

Poll: "¿Te pasó?" — "ME PASÓ" / "LO SABÍA" / "SOY EL SUEGRO".

Loop: the last picture (the whole circle from above) echoes the first.
